# T3 Code

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code)), [web app](https://app.t3.codes) and [Electron-based desktop app](https://t3.codes).

Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

## "Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

## Installation

> [!WARNING]
> T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, and fx. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:
>
> - Codex: install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`
> - Claude: install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`
> - Cursor: install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli) and run `agent login`
> - Grok Build: install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli) and run `grok login`
> - OpenCode: install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and run `opencode auth login`
> - Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use **Install Antigravity** and **Sign in with Google**. No CLI is required.
> - fx: install [fx](https://fx.sh) and run `fx login` on the machine running the T3 Code server ([setup guide](./docs/user/providers-fx.md))

# agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: read and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree.

A CLI and C library for macOS, Windows and Linux. A snapshot returns JSON with a ref for every element an agent can act on. The agent acts on a ref and snapshots again to check, with no pixel matching; the loop stays in your agent. Every CLI call runs in its own process. Headless calls still prohibit foreground activation and synthesized input. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. The optional [JEV helper](skills/jev-desktop/SKILL.md) sends screen descriptions to a configured model provider; it is separate from the native CLI. See [privacy and data handling](docs/faq.md#what-data-can-contain-private-information). ## Installation Install on macOS, Windows or Linux with npm: ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop version ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. # Handy

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-%235865F2.svg?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.com/invite/WVBeWsNXK4)

**A free, open source, and extensible speech-to-text application that works completely offline.**

Handy is a cross-platform desktop application that provides simple, privacy-focused speech transcription. Press a shortcut, speak, and have your words appear in any text field. This happens on your own computer without sending any information to the cloud.

## Why Handy?

Handy was created to fill the gap for a truly open source, extensible speech-to-text tool. As stated on [handy.computer](https://handy.computer):

- **Free**: Accessibility tooling belongs in everyone's hands, not behind a paywall
- **Open Source**: Together we can build further. Extend Handy for yourself and contribute to something bigger
- **Private**: Your voice stays on your computer. Get transcriptions without sending audio to the cloud
- **Simple**: One tool, one job. Transcribe what you say and put it into a text box

## How It Works

1. **Press** a configurable keyboard shortcut: hold it to record and release to stop, or tap it to toggle recording on and off (Hold-only and Toggle-only modes are also available)
2. **Speak** your words while the shortcut is active
3. **Release** and Handy processes your speech using Whisper
4. **Get** your transcribed text pasted directly into whatever app you're using

The process is entirely local:

- Silence is filtered using VAD (Voice Activity Detection) with Silero
- Transcription uses your choice of models:
  - **Whisper models** (Small/Medium/Turbo/Large) with GPU acceleration when available
  - **Parakeet V3** - CPU-optimized model with excellent performance and automatic language detection
- Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux

# nanochat

![nanochat logo](dev/nanochat.png)
![scaling laws](dev/scaling_laws_jan26.png)

nanochat is the simplest experimental harness for training LLMs. It is designed to run on a single GPU node, the code is minimal/hackable, and it covers all major LLM stages including tokenization, pretraining, finetuning, evaluation, and inference. For example, you can train your own GPT-2 capability LLM (which cost ~$43,000 to train in 2019) for only $48 (~2 hours of 8XH100 GPU node) and then talk to it over a simple CLI. On a spot instance, the total cost can be closer to ~$15. More generally, nanochat is configured out of the box to train an entire miniseries of compute-optimal models by setting one single complexity dial: `--depth`, the number of layers in the GPT transformer model (GPT-2 capability happens to be approximately depth 26). All other hyperparameters (the width of the transformer, number of heads, learning rate adjustments, training horizons, weight decays, ...) are calculated automatically in an optimal way.

For questions about the repo, I recommend either using [DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/karpathy/nanochat) from Devin/Cognition to ask questions about the repo, or use the [Discussions tab](https://github.com/karpathy/nanochat/discussions), or come by the [#nanochat](https://discord.com/channels/1020383067459821711/1427295580895314031) channel on Discord.

## Time-to-GPT-2 Leaderboard

Presently, the main focus of development is on tuning the pretraining stage, which takes the most amount of compute. # wifit3 > A standalone USB Wi-Fi auditor for Linux, Windows, and macOS.

> *At least* one of the [supported USB adapters](#supported-hardware) is **required**. ## Why? * **Cross-Platform:** Runs identically on Linux, macOS, and Windows. * **Wireless Driver Heaven:** Built-in wireless stack avoids kernel driver versioning hell and Windows' NDIS. * **Zero Runtime Dependencies:** No `aircrack-ng` or `reaver`, just pure Python with PyUSB & Textual libraries.

# scriptc

scriptc compiles TypeScript and JavaScript to native executables and WebAssembly. It uses the types checked by the TypeScript compiler to generate machine code, and the output runs without Node.js installed. npm packages your program imports compile along with it. Code scriptc can't compile is reported at build time with a diagnostic and, where available, a rewrite hint. scriptc is experimental and supports a subset of JavaScript, TypeScript, and Node.js APIs. readme_excerpt:
# Kero

A terminal for coding agents, on macOS, Windows and Linux.

Run Claude Code, Codex, a dev server or a test watcher each in its own session. Kero groups sessions by project in a sidebar that shows which are working, which need you and which are done.

- **Sessions outlive the window.** They run in `kerod`, a small daemon, so quitting Kero leaves them running. Reopen it and every pane and its scrollback is back.
- **Status at a glance.** Each pane is working, waiting, idle, error or exited. <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>J</kbd> jumps to the one that needs you, and Kero notifies you when an agent finishes, fails or is blocked.
- **A CLI agents can drive.** `kero` starts sessions, splits panes, types into them, waits on them and reads their screens.
- **Remote hosts.** Run agents on a Linux box, a cloud VM, a Mac, a Windows PC or WSL and see them in the same sidebar, over SSH or Tailscale. They keep running when your laptop sleeps. See [Remote Hosts](docs/remote.md).
- **Ghostty under the hood.** Terminals render with libghostty, so Ghostty themes, fonts and config keys just work.

## Install

Download Kero from the [releases page](https://github.com/egoist/kero/releases), then choose **Kero › Install Command Line Tool…** to put `kero` on your `PATH`.

```sh
kero new -n fix-login -- claude
```

To run sessions on a Linux server, a Mac or a Windows PC, install the server build there, then add the machine in **Settings › Hosts**:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/egoist/kero/releases/latest/download/install-server.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/egoist/kero/releases/latest/download/install-server.ps1 | iex
```

See the [docs](docs/index.md) for more.

## Prior art

- [**Rex**](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/installation): Mitchell Hashimoto's terminal and multiplexer in one native app, with sessions that persist through a server and a scriptable CLI.
- [**Herdr**](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr): a terminal multiplexe
